claims.source_ref:
3D-Printed Limbs: Body Parts That Don't Cost an Arm and a Leg

When Alex Pring was born in Florida without most of his right arm, it seemed that his life would never be like that of other children. However, Alex's life changed when engineering student at a university in the US collaborated to give him a hand. They developed a plastic electronic arm equipped with a sensor that would enable Alex to open and close his hand by slightly flexing his biceps muscle. Now, Alex can use both arms to hug his parents. With 3D printing technology, artificial limbs can be produced relatively cheaply, which promises to benefit people like Alex in ways that they never dreamed possible.
